episodes.173301: A persistent upper-level trough lingered over the FL peninsula while the low-level trough axis was inland across NE FL.  NE flow on the 'west' side of the trough axis was steering numerous showers with embedded thunderstorms to the SW across inland NE FL, some producing training locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.173439: Supercells developed ahead and along of surface trough producing widespread hail reports and some damaging wind gusts.
episodes.173440: Supercells developed ahead and along of surface trough producing widespread hail reports and some damaging wind gusts.
episodes.174040: A shortwave trough supplied enough moisture and weak lift to sustain non sever convection through much of the morning of September 17th. By evening a secondary lobe of low pressure lifted into Iowa, enhancing convective development. MLCAPE over 2000 J/kg, curve hodographs, and steep mid level lapse rates supported large hail development. Convection lasted much of the evening and overnight across southern Iowa with several of the multicell storms producing severe hail. In addition, storms produced pockets of heavy rain with area receiving three to five inches of rain.
episodes.174128: A cold front moving across northern Minnesota the evening of the 17th led to the development of storms across the region. A few of the storms were marginally severe in the Brainerd Lakes area bringing isolated reports of 1 inch diameter hail and some wind damage in a few of the storms. One business near Pequot Lakes received roof damage from the winds of a decaying storm.
episodes.174159: A series of storms moved across central Kansas producing severe winds up to 90 mph in some locations.  Many reports of wind damage were noted particularly in the Saline County vicinity.  Other areas had to dodge large hail as many locations reported hail up ot the size of golf balls.
episodes.174286: A stalled front over North Florida in combination with an upper level low pressure over South Florida led to an unstable atmosphere and the developed of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms near and offshore the Atlantic coast of SE Florida.
episodes.174475: An upper level jet diving down the coast of California, combined with plentiful lower level moisture advected from the Pacific set the stage for an early season rain storm and strong winds around much of the Bay Area and Central Coast. The highest winds occurred along the coast, where various sites reported gusts between 35 and 50 mph. A wind advisory was in effect from early Sunday morning through Sunday evening for the immediate coast and coastal hills. Highest rainfall totals were recorded in the coastal mountains from Sonoma County southward through Big Sur, resulting in localized flooding, downed trees/powerlines and debris/rocks sliding onto Highway 1 in Big Sur. A flood advisory was issued for a large portion of the Monterey Bay coastal zone and Big Sur coast from late night on the 18th through early morning on the 19th. Storm Total Rainfall measured 2 to 3.5 inches in North Bay Coastal Mountains, 1.5 to 2.2 inches in the Santa Cruz Mountains and 2 to 4.7 inches in the Santa Lucia's. Lower totals closer to an inch or less were recorded around the SF Bay Shoreline and coastal Monterey Bay.
episodes.174484: An afternoon isolated supercell produced hail and damaging wind on 9/17, followed by redevelopment of scattered storms during the evening which produced more severe weather. Winds to 70 mph were observed. One additional cluster of storms developed overnight into 9/18 and produced more hail.
episodes.174544: Hurricane Fiona made landfall on Sunday the 18th around 3:20 PM AST near Punta Toc��n in southwestern Puerto Rico.  Strong, gusty winds accompanied much of the stronger convection embedded within the hurricane. Hurricane-force gusts were observed over portions of southern Puerto Rico during the afternoon on Sunday. These gusty winds, combined with ground saturation, resulted in damage across the island due to fallen trees and power lines. ||Fiona resulted in excessive rainfall, especially for southern into eastern Puerto Rico.  In areas along the Cordillera and around El Yunque, widespread rainfall totals of over 16 inches were seen, most of which fell on Sunday. Preliminary estimates suggest that over 24 inches of rain were seen locally, mostly around Cayey and southern Caguas and Aibonito to southern Jayuya. Multiple rivers in eastern Puerto Rico, mostly those that had been most affected by the previous week���s rain, reached major flooding. Widespread flooding was reported, mostly in southern and central Puerto Rico. Numerous mudslides were also reported throughout the affected areas of steep terrain.
